content.source_line: motion-blur.md L14 — 高速に回転する物体をストロボ的に撮影すると、止まっているように見えたり、逆方向に動いているかのように見えてしまう

physics.shutter: 360 deg (full frame interval, centered on the frame time)
physics.blur_method: in-composition accumulation: 80 sub-frame copies at opacity 1/80 composited with mix-blend-mode: plus-lighter over black = exact arithmetic mean (box filter). blade fill 240/255 so 240/80 = 3.0 exactly per 8-bit channel
physics.ramp: linear 0 -> 15 rev/s in both passes; 15 s of it in the crisp pass, the same sweep replayed in 9 s in the blurred pass
physics.aliasing_derivation: fps/blades = 8 rev/s = 120deg/frame = one whole pattern period, so the crisp pass is dead still only at 8 rev/s. Half that, 4 rev/s = 60deg/frame, is Nyquist: the blades jump back and forth and direction is lost, and again at 12 rev/s whose 180deg/frame folds to 60deg. The landmarks sit at fixed speeds, so they fall at t=4.0/8.0/12.0s in the 15 s crisp pass and t=2.4/4.8/7.2s in the 9 s blurred pass. Between 4 and 8 rev/s the propeller reads as running backwards. The ramp ends at 15 rev/s = 225deg/frame, folding to -15deg: a 1 rev/s backwards crawl at full speed.

acts.beat: No motion blur, held for 15 s so every aliasing landmark can be read. Propeller ramps linearly 0 -> 15 rev/s: direction is lost at 4 rev/s, it runs visibly backwards from 4 to 8, goes dead still at 8, reads forwards again, loses direction once more at 12, and ends crawling backwards at an apparent 1 rev/s.

Motion blur. The same 0 -> 15 rev/s sweep replayed in 9 s — the answer needs less screen time than the question — integrated over a 360deg shutter: the smear grows with the real speed, the backwards crawl and the false freeze are gone, and at 8 rev/s and above the propeller is an honest uniform disc.
